stories.headline: Champions League Power Rankings before MD5: Who's No. 1?
stories.summary: The UEFA Champions League is going at full speed, and we're beyond the halfway point of the league phase. Injuries are starting to pile up. Where does your club rank?
stories.body:
We're officially past the midway point of the UEFA Champions League league phase as the 2026-27 European season rumbles on, and the grind of the calendar is beginning to take its toll on the elite teams, with injuries starting to pile up. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Désiré Doué (Paris Saint-Germain) and David Raya (Arsenal) were all sidelined this weekend with issues of varying severity, and it's only going to get more grueling as we head toward the hectic festive period and, beyond that, the January transfer window.

So what has it done to the standings? Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.

UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 5

1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN (no change)

- Previous rank: 1

- Games since MD3: defeated Lyon 2-0; defeated Le Havre 5-1; defeated Villarreal 6-0; defeated Troyes 1-0; defeated Nice 3-2

- MD5 opponent: vs. AS Roma (Wednesday)

Would anyone bet against them winning it all a third straight time? Our voters were nearly unanimous -- 15 of 17 -- in crowning the French champions and back-to-back Champions League winners as the best team in this competition, but there are tough tests to come.

PSG continue to look sharp and ruthless domestically, which isn't normally their rhythm at this time of year. (Folks will remember that they generally wake up, form-wise, after Christmas, at least in recent seasons.) Ferran Torres keeps showing why he was such a savvy summer signing from Barcelona, chipping in eight goals and an assist as an occasional starter, with the likes of Senny Mayulu -- one of 12 players to get on the score sheet in Ligue 1 this season -- also stepping up to contribute in the attacking third.

They were managing without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who tore his ACL in October and faces a lengthy spell on the sideline, but Saturday's season-ending knee injury suffered by Doué in this weekend's win over Nice will tax their reserves over the course of a grueling campaign. Up next is a potentially tricky midweek date with Roma who, despite losing to Man United in Matchday 4, have one of the stingiest defenses in Serie A (11 goals conceded in 12 games).

2. BARCELONA (no change)

- Previous rank: 2

- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Real Madrid; defeated Alaves 6-1; defeated Aston Villa 3-0; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-1; defeated Villarreal 3-2

- MD5 opponent: at Sabah FK (Wednesday)

The Spanish champions continue to be box-office entertainment every week. They simply do not believe in drawing games; every single one of their games this season has ended with a decisive winner and loser, with their back-to-back losses to PSG and Real Madrid surrounded by wins up and down the schedule. Since the Clasico setback it has largely been business as usual, with big wins over Alaves and Villa followed by a very different pair of comeback victories at Atletico and home to Villarreal. Sunday's win had the feel of a predator toying with its prospective dinner, as Villarreal scored twice in the opening seven minutes to daze Lamine Yamal & Co. early, only for the champs to respond with three goals in 10 second-half minutes and a three-point lead at the top of LaLiga.

Like PSG, they have a simmering injury concern to their defensive corps, with several front-line defenders in various stages of rehab or treatment: Andreas Christensen has managed just 30 minutes of game time since mid-September, Pau Cubarsí's health is being monitored after a hip injury on international duty, and Jules Koundé/Eric García are just coming back from absences of their own. Rodri's ongoing fitness is a worry too as the best choice to shield a vulnerable back line, but as long as they are scoring goals by the bucketload -- their 51 in 13 LaLiga games is more than the bottom four teams in the table combined -- it feels like a minor concern. That said, Hansi Flick's side will need to tighten up once we get into the business end of this competition.

3. ARSENAL (no change)

- Previous rank: 3

- Games since MD3: defeated Everton 2-0; lost 5-3 on penalties vs. Fleetwood Town (Carabao Cup); defeated Liverpool 1-0; defeated Slavia Prague 2-1; defeated Hull 1-0; drew 2-2 vs. Newcastle

- MD5 opponent: vs. Borussia Dortmund (Tuesday)

The Gunners already have a six-point lead atop the Premier League after just 11 games, which feels like business as usual for Mikel Arteta's side, but the manner in which they slumped to a draw at Newcastle on Saturday shows that this side isn't quite at the juggernaut levels it achieved last season. Their aggressive press yielded the opening goal, when Kai Havertz snagged the ball from Lewis Hall and teed up Eberechi Eze, but Noni Madueke whiffed before halftime to double their lead and Arsenal crumbled after the break, conceding twice. Noni Madueke eventually atoned by rifling in the equalizer, but the loss of control and absence of ruthlessness will have Arsenal's rivals on notice.

This week's visit of Dortmund has all the hallmarks of a trap game, considering BVB are having a superb season so far and Arteta will have one eye on next weekend's visit of Man City to the Emirates instead. Shrugging off Saturday's torpor and asserting dominance over Niko Kovac & Co. on Tuesday will be essential to demoralizing the chasing pack.

4. REAL MADRID (up 2)

- Previous rank: 6

- Games since MD3: defeated Barcelona 2-1; defeated Racing Santander 3-0; defeated AEK Athens 3-2; defeated Valencia 3-0; defeated Celta Vigo 2-1

- MD5 opponent: vs. PSV Eindhoven (Tuesday)

Since Jose Mourinho announced his return to the Bernabeu this summer, we've been wondering when things would start to come apart at the seams. All the ingredients were present: a grouchy manager with a chip on his shoulder and no filter, a star-studded but temperamental squad in need of careful coaching, a demanding fanbase that's impatient for success after a couple of seasons without silverware. And yet, everything looks kinda good at the moment? They won the Clasico, are unbeaten since Sept. 20's Madrid derby, and Mourinho is managing his way out of sticky situations with smart substitutions, canny motivation and a sense of calm we've not really seen from him to date.

However, you can see cracks here and there -- it took some inspired second-half subs to overcome Celta Vigo, who scored first -- and Mourinho will need to be gentle in how he keeps his attacking corps happy. Vinicius Jr. is back from suspension (and a nice international break with Brazil), and will be keen for playing time regardless of how well Yan Diomande, Arda Güler, Carlos Espí and Jude Bellingham have looked in support of Kylian Mbappé.

Mourinho's magic and the relative stability/fitness have vaulted them into the top four of our rankings for the first time this season; will it stick?

5. BAYERN MUNICH (down 1)

- Previous rank: 4

- Games since MD3: defeated Freiburg 3-1; defeated Magdeburg 6-1; drew 2-2 vs. Borussia Dortmund; defeated Atletico Madrid 2-0; defeated Mainz 2-1; drew 1-1 vs. Koln

- MD5 opponent: at Lille (Wednesday)

Bayern continue to chug along domestically -- wobble in Der Klassiker aside -- but the injuries to Kane and Michael Olise in Friday's draw with Koln will hurt their chances of keeping up with their rivals in the Champions League. Kane won't be back for months after ankle surgery, while Olise (bruised foot) joins the likes of Luis Díaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry in the ranks of hobbled playmakers, all of which will test manager Vincent Kompany's abilities over the coming weeks.

The traditional Bundesliga "winterpause" means it won't hurt them much domestically, but our voters have downgraded them in the context of the Champions League until they figure out some viable alternatives.

6. MANCHESTER CITY (down 1)

- Previous rank: 5

- Games since MD3: lost 2-1 vs. Aston Villa; defeated Brighton 4-3 on penalties (Carabao Cup); lost 1-0 vs. Brighton; defeated RB Leipzig 3-2; lost 3-1 vs. Nottingham Forest; drew 1-1 vs. Fulham

- MD5 opponent: vs. Napoli (Tuesday)

Things have not been going well for Enzo Maresca & Co. in recent weeks, with dropped points in the Premier League and a slew of bereft, listless performances regardless of results. Are we finally seeing the toll of the Premier League's charges -- with the appeals and punishments processes happening on parallel timelines since the news broke at the end of September -- on this squad and these players? There's a fog around the Etihad, one in which their identity, effectiveness and performance are struggling to be seen.

The midfield has been a mess since Rodri left for Barcelona, with Elliot Anderson (who scored a superb goal in the draw vs. Fulham) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (only 19) still figuring out how to mesh with Enzo Fernández and the passel of high-class attackers further ahead. The defense is also creaking in the worst ways, with Rúben Dias looking vulnerable and only the occasional heroics from Gianluigi Donnarumma keeping them in games.

There's no need to panic yet, but the fans are restless, the uncertainty around their potential punishments is overwhelming, and the vibes are sour. However, our voters still see them as a credible contender in Europe given the raw talent up and down the roster; if they can harness some momentum and secure a top-eight finish (and first-round playoff bye) in the Champions League, they can still make a deep, impactful run.

7. LIVERPOOL (no change)

- Previous rank: 7

- Games since MD3: defeated Brighton 2-0; defeated Chelsea 6-5 on penalties (Carabao Cup); lost 1-0 vs. Arsenal; lost 3-2 vs. Fenerbahce; defeated Crystal Palace 3-1; defeated Manchester United 4-0

- MD5 opponent: at Club Brugge (Wednesday)

Liverpool have looked better and more effective in the Champions League this season -- Fenerbahce defeat aside -- given that their playmakers generally have more time and space on the ball in Europe, but the Reds are turning the corner domestically as well. After months of two-steps-forward-one-step-back form and results, Andoni Iraola's vision is starting to take shape.

It's been far from linear progress, of course -- Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have all scored in recent games despite also looking completely peripheral in others -- and the optimal midfield combination has yet to be figured out, but the defensive platform provided by Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Jérémy Jacquet has brought a welcome stability to a team that leaked goals all of last season. Ronald Araujo has won hearts and minds at Anfield, too, with the all-gas, no-brakes manner in which he insists on covering every inch of grass, and Rio Ngumoha continues to dazzle with skills and impact far beyond his years.

A tough run of league fixtures will take them into the always hectic festive period, but they will need to show the same ruthlessness against Club Brugge in midweek that they showed against Man United on Sunday.

8. COMO (new)

- Previous rank: N/R

- Games since MD3: defeated Sassuolo 2-0; defeated Torino 3-1; defeated Venezia 1-0; defeated Lens 9-1; lost 2-0 vs. Inter Milan; defeated Cagliari 2-0

- MD5 opponent: vs. AEK Athens (Tuesday)

It seems crazy that only now, as we approach the end of November, are Como making it into our Power Rankings. It's not for me to say if our collective disrespect is serving as motivational material for Cesc Fabregas & Co. or not, but the Italian upstarts are fully deserving of a spot among the tournament favorites. If the nine-goal game against Lens didn't do it for you, what about them having an 8-2-2 record in Serie A with a squad averaging under 26 years old per player?

Fabregas is shaping up to be the next big thing in coaching based on how he's taking this tiny tourist town team from the sporting doldrums and into the spotlight, with Nico Paz the straw stirring the drink in attacking midfield to make it all click. He's got a ton of help, too -- Anastasios Douvikas is no household name but has 11 goals in 16 games, while Martin Baturina and Maximo Perrone are clever contributors -- and their press-heavy, quick-passing style is overwhelming opponents in all competitions.

It's too early to admit them to European soccer's highest tier, but they can make waves in the Champions League with a favorable draw and a clean bill of health across their squad.

9. INTER MILAN (no change)

- Previous rank: 9

- Games since MD3: defeated Fiorentina 2-1; defeated Venezia 2-0; lost 3-1 vs. AC Milan; defeated Feyenoord 3-0; defeated Como 2-0; drew 4-4 vs. Atalanta

- MD5 opponent: vs. Stuttgart (Wednesday)

Inter Milan are an Italian institution and the defending Serie A champions, but they rank below Como heading into Matchday 5! Our voters aren't quite convinced that Cristian Chivu's side has what it takes to contend for the Champions League right now -- Inter were runners-up in 2024-25 as PSG claimed their first, only to fall in the knockout phase play-off round to Bodo/Glimt, which may be weighing heavy on our electorate. If that didn't do it, Sunday's stunning draw at struggling Atalanta, in which they let 3-1 and 4-2 leads slip away with a litany of individual errors -- will have soured them to whether this team has what it takes.

The bright spot right now is Pio Esposito, who has scored eight goals in his last five games for club and country, and with Lautaro Martínez coming back to full fitness, Inter has enough firepower to blow most opponents away. But Chivu needs his team to tighten up quick before they lose sight of the Serie A leaders (Inter are third after 12 games) and the points gap in the Champions League becomes too big to overcome down the stretch.

10. ATLÉTICO MADRID (down 2)

- Previous rank: 8

- Games since MD3: defeated Deportivo Coruna 2-1; defeated Levante 2-0; lost 2-0 vs. Bayern Munich; lost 2-1 vs. Barcelona, defeated Getafe 3-0

- MD5 opponent: vs. Viking (Wednesday)

Diego Simeone's side is losing the games you'd expect it to (Bayern, Barca) and picking up points everywhere else, which feels par for the course for LaLiga's third-biggest team. Despite being 23rd of 36 teams at the UCL midway point, with just four points (and one win) to their name, Atleti's pedigree still resonates among our voters when it comes the Power Rankings.

Sunday's win over Getafe was a milestone for Simeone -- his 345th win makes him LaLiga's all-time winningest manager -- and showcased the electricity in his squad that still makes voters feel so fondly for the talent. Julián Álvarez hasn't scored for Atleti in over a month but notched two assists this weekend as the de facto center forward, Álex Baena has made the wing position his own, and U.S. midfielder Johnny Cardoso also found the net.

Dropped out: Aston Villa

Other teams receiving votes

Borussia Dortmund, AS Roma, Aston Villa, Sporting CP, Man United

VOTERS

Our global panel includes writers and editors around FC and our global soccer desks: Tony Mabert, Jon Molyneux-Carter, Alex Kirkland, Bill Connelly, Tom Hamilton, Armando Neria, Rob Dawson, Nicholas Som, Austin Lindberg, Gustavo Hofman, James Tyler, Gab Marcotti, Mariano Mancuso, James Olley, Sam Marsden and Beth Lindop.

stories.headline: Fantasy risers and fallers: Trade Davion Mitchell? Move on from De'Aaron Fox?
stories.summary: Steve Alexander looks at three players on the rise and three who are slumping and how fantasy managers should react.
stories.body:
Davion Mitchell is turning heads and leading the league in assists, Quentin Grimes is on a heater in Los Angeles and Cedric Coward is quickly emerging as a fantasy force. All are moving up the fantasy rankings.

Meanwhile, Kel'el Ware's stint for the 1-16 Bucks has been a nightmare, Jalen Green is not pulling his weight in Phoenix and De'Aaron Fox has really struggled in San Antonio. Which ones should you move on from at this point?

Risers and Fallers helps you track hot players who are worth holding onto, players are are likely overvalued right now (see the final paragraph under Risers), as well as struggling players you might be better off without. Here's more on each of these players.

Resources: Rankings | Adds/Drops | Scoring leaders | Player Rater | Mock draft lobby | Depth charts | Schedule | Injuries

Risers
Davion Mitchell, Heat PG, (86.8% rostered in ESPN leagues)
Mitchell was drafted around the 10th round in most of my 12-team drafts and he's shocking the world, leading the league in assists and appearing to love playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo. His November numbers include 17.5 points, 8.9 assists, 1.4 steals, 0.7 blocks and 2.7 triples, while hitting 52.6% of his shots.

This might seem to scream "trade him before the bottom falls out," but I don't think that's the case. You likely drafted him very late in your draft (or even got him off the waiver wire) and he's also been one of your best players all season. Especially over the last two weeks, when he's been a Top 10 fantasy player. I'm holding onto Mitchell until further notice and I think he's very driven to win the assist title this season. And with guys like Bam Adebayo and Giannis to throw it to, he should continue to do this all year. Ride the wave.

Quentin Grimes, Lakers SG/SF, (45.7% rostered)

I sadly wrote that Sandro Mamukelashvili was a Riser last week, but things have changed a lot since then. Grimes has been on fire with Austin Reaves (heel) and Luka Doncic (rest) missing games, but that's not the main reason he's cooking right now.

He scored 22 points last Sunday and then exploded for a career-high 47 against Charlotte on Tuesday. He then scored 20 and 13 points in each of his last two games and is averaging a ridiculous 25.5 points, 5.0 3-pointers, 6.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists over his last four.

Sure, he'll take a hit once Reaves is back, but the Lakers are going to be careful with Reaves and we've already seen them give Luka and Walker Kessler the occasional night off. But the most important point here is that I suspect Luka has figured out the Lakers are a better team when Grimes is cooking, and he's become his new go-to guy after Reaves and Kessler, shoving Mamukelashvili out of the way. And that means that Grimes should be a solid fantasy player all season. If you've got him, hang onto him rather than trying to capitalize on his recent success. Hopefully, he's just getting started.

Cedric Coward, Grizzlies SG/SF, 75% rostered
Coward is becoming a force and reminds me a little of Dylan Harper, who's out with a hip injury right now for the Spurs. Going into Saturday's game, Coward was coming off a fun four-game run that resulted in 20 points, 6.8 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 1.5 steals, 1.0 blocks and 3.8 3-pointers with excellent shooting from everywhere.

He's been playing well all year and while I knew he was an intriguing prospect, I didn't expect him to be this good this fast. He's also a big reason the Grizzlies are 12-5 (along with Ty Jerome, Cameron Boozer and Cam Spencer) and they're going to continue to build the team around him (and Boozer) going forward. The Grizzlies want to make the playoffs and do some damage while they're there, and Coward is going to be a force for the rest of the season, assuming he stays healthy.

Bonus tip
If you're looking for some hot players to deal while their trade value is high, James Harden (out of his mind on Friday), Franz Wagner (before Paolo Banchero returns), Anthony Davis (before he gets hurt) and Klay Thompson (before he runs out of gas) probably fit the bill.

Fallers
Kel'el Ware, Bucks C, (50.7% rostered)
Ware's minutes have been highly inconsistent and he's been one of the more disappointing players I drafted this year. And, unfortunately, that was in a ton of leagues. I'm not giving up hope just yet, as there's still a chance the Bucks will eventually give up on the season and start developing their young players. And Ware's ability to score, board, steal, block and shoot the 3-pointer is nothing to sneeze at.

Despite a 50-point explosion from Tyler Herro on Saturday, they still lost to the Sixers and are now 1-16 on the season. I really don't understand the point of running Kyle Kuzma, Myles Turner and Herro out there for 35 minutes every night when young players like Ware, Brayden Burries, Ryan Rollins and Kasparas Jakucionis need some of those minutes. If your league is 10 teams or less, Ware might be droppable. But in 12-team leagues, I'm still hanging onto Ware, who had six points, eight boards, a steal and a block on Saturday. That said, if things are still going like this in a month, I might have to check out.

Jalen Green, Suns SG/SF, (60.8% rostered)
I think Green is fine to hold in leagues that are 14-teams and larger, but he's droppable in 12-team leagues, and is especially not worth having in smaller ones (10 or eight teams, etc.). He has the ability to be an elite scorer, but is averaging just 12.5 points on the season, is shooting fantasy teams into oblivion with his 41.8% from the field and 70.5% from the line, and is at just 0.9 steals, 0.4 blocks and 1.2 3-pointers.

Green may get traded, but either way, it feels like the Suns are either looking for a true point guard (Dejounte Murray?) or may just start rolling with Collin Gillespie. The bottom line is that his name is bigger than his game and I'm not sure Green's ever going to become a fantasy must-have player. And, so far, he's barely even worth rostering this year, if at all.

De'Aaron Fox, Spurs PG, (92.9% rostered)
I'm not sure what's going on with Fox, but entering Saturday night, he was averaging just 10.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.7 3-pointers on 40% shooting. And in his three games before that, those numbers dipped even further, including zero 3-pointers made and 29% shooting. Then he scored just five points on Saturday.

Add in the fact that he didn't see a boost after Harper (hip) went down, and this is another concern. The Spurs are deep, Harper and Stephon Castle have a high usage rate (not to mention Victor Wembanyama), and Fox is basically just a facilitator of the offense and nothing more, at least for now. I'm thinking you let him break out of the funk and post a big game or two, and then look into moving him. Once Harper is back, Fox is not going to be a priority for San Antonio on the offensive end of things. Then again, he hasn't been that all season, with or without Harper.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: I could have beaten Kimi Antonelli if I was Ferrari No. 1
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.

Hamilton's claim arrived after he tangled with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix -- a flashpoint Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur described as "completely unacceptable." Leclerc was sanctioned by the stewards for his role in the collision.

Hamilton's maiden win for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona took him 41 points behind Antonelli, and 40 ahead of Leclerc.

And although Hamilton rejected the notion that he ever called on Ferrari to make him its number one driver, the 41-year-old suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have afforded Antonelli a proper run for his money.

"I've never asked to be the number one," Hamilton said. "I genuinely haven't. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead [of Leclerc] and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi.

"I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi.

"There were a few instances in the season -- where, with the support -- I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle.

"It's not what I've asked for. But we shouldn't have been able to come together [in Las Vegas]. It should just never happen. I've said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari."

Hamilton's chances of finishing runner-up in the standings -- his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 -- now look shot following the Dutch driver's brilliant recent form.

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift.

Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on teammate Antonelli for second backfired.

"I wanted that win," Russell said. "It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price.

"Of course I'm disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps."

stories.headline: Way-too-early look ahead to the 2027 AFL Draft: 15 players to know
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years with the introduction of Tasmania. Who are the players to know? Jasper Chellappah has named 15 to keep an eye on next year.
stories.body:
On to the next.

The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years, with Tasmania's inclusion making for an expansion draft similar to that of 2010 and 2011. The Devils own picks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13 in the first round, plus the first pick of each subsequent round as part of concessions.

The club will need to trade 5, 7, 11, and 13 or roll them into 2028 or 2029. That means the competition's 19th team will take 1, 3 and 9 to the draft next year.

Tasmania has also pre-listed some of the brightest talents in the crop. Axel Walsh, Baxter Sruk, and Jake Miller were all clear pick No. 1 contenders 12 months out from their draft, and will attend school in Hobart and play football in the VFL next year.

Five Tasmania-tied teens have been included in the ones to watch next year. Another three are club-tied, making 2027 the most compromised draft in AFL history. Twenty-three of the 46 prospects in the AFL Futures exhibition on Grand Final day were club-tied.

Perhaps the saving grace for 18 other clubs is the fact that 2027 has been touted as an elite draft class for some time. There's premium talent still in the open pool and another 12 months for more quality to emerge, with a heavy leaning towards midfielders.

With an extended 15 prospects given the club-tied nature of the class, this is ESPN's way-too-early look ahead to the best prospects in the 2027 AFL Draft.

1. Axel Walsh (Tasmania pre-list)

East Perth/Western Australia

RUC, 201cm

Another in the resurgence of premium ruck prospects in the draft, and perhaps the best. Walsh is a monster in the air; his best traits come with his aerial strength where he drifts back to intercept mark, pushes forward to stretch defences and dominates around the ground. He will fill out to become a true ruck size and is as close to Max Gawn as a prospect has been this decade. Walsh would be the pick one favourite if he wasn't pre-listed by Tasmania.

2. Baxter Sruk (Tasmania pre-list)

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID, 185cm

Sruk has been a big game performer and consistent midfield standout in the Talent League. He's a physical on-baller that throws his weight around, impacts with his ball-winning and gets forward to kick goals in bunches. Sruk thrives in the heat of the contest and brings tenacity to Tasmania's list.

3. Jake Miller (Tasmania pre-list)

Western Jets/Vic Metro

FWD, 197cm

Miller is the leading key forward prospect next year. He enjoyed a stellar national championships as a bottom-ager, named to the All-Australian team as well as the Talent League All-Australian side. Miller is a brilliant mark with arms outstretched, able to take big contested marks in packs and secure the ball on long searching leads. He's a reliable set shot off his left foot and is an elite runner for his size. Tasmania has already pre-listed the immense talent.

4. Max Thompson

Bendigo Pioneers/Vic Country

FWD/MID, 175cm

Thompson has played in varying positions and looked good but is clearly at his best inside 50. He's smart and crafty, puts speed on the game and is a wonderfully fluid kick of the ball. Thompson can get up the ground and beat his man back to goals, distribute off halfback or win his own ball. He's the type of versatile small forward that clubs will covet.

5. James Artemis

East Fremantle/Western Australia

MID, 177cm

A leading contender in the open pool, Artemis is the cousin of Essendon's Jaxon and will have suitors very early in the draft. He's a hard-nosed contested midfielder that can then link up transition with hard running and slick ball use. He's dogged with the ball up for grabs and then powers through contact to get it moving forward.

6. Koby Bewick (Essendon father-son)

Calder Cannons/Vic Metro

MID, 178cm

Modern footy suits Bewick down to the ground. The son of 1993 and 2000 premiership small forward Darren, the Calder midfielder has been thrown around in different positions but has all the traits to become an excellent on-baller. He's incisive with his movement and foot skills on the outside, and possesses the running base and work ethic to rack up a lot of the ball in transition. He comes alive in open space where he can run and carry and pick out targets inside 50, which could see him start his career off halfback or a wing. Bewick kicked two goals from 19 touches in his Futures outing.

7. Zemes Pilot (Port Adelaide NGA)

South Adelaide/South Australia

FWD/MID, 193cm

Pilot is an elite basketball talent as well, so it's a coup for footy that the 193cm forward is opting to pursue opportunities in Port's NGA. The uber-athletic tall forward is incredible to watch, soaring above packs to take epic marks, breaking ankles with sharp agility and kicking goals from ridiculous angles. He had a game last year in the SANFL U16s with 27 disposals and 9.4 in front of goals.

8. Jett Flower

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID/DEF, 183cm

Flower is the grandson of Melbourne legend Robbie, and one of the top open pool prospects in 2027. Boasting one of the best names to come through the pathways in some time, Flower is a classy outside midfielder with beautiful foot skills and a strong running base. He likely appeals to clubs as a rebounder out of defence with his competitiveness a feature behind the ball. Flower was best afield in the Futures game with 17 disposals and a goal.

9. Louis Salopek (Port Adelaide father-son)

Dandenong Stingrays/Vic Country

MID/FWD, 186cm

A genuine star of the crop, Salopek has been in the wars across the past year or so, enduring three separate incidents of a collapsed lung. He burst onto the scene for Vic Country in the U16s champs and plays with a high motor, tackling and pressuring through the midfield and pushing forward to hit the scoreboard. He's keen to get to the Power as the son of Steven.

10. Riley Stratford (Tasmania pre-list)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 188cm

A taller midfielder who still needs to build into his frame, Stratford has been part of some massive games in his junior career. He was a star for Brighton Grammar on the way to an inaugural APS title and can play on a wing or through the engine room with impact in the air. Tasmania has locked him away and he'll play for their VFL side next year.

11. Oscar Henwood

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

MID, 185cm

Henwood was a key contributor in the Power's Talent League flag and plays with great composure. He can try to bite off too much with his time in possession but is typically creative and uses it really well in space.

12. Harvey Chapman

Sturt/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

Chapman is the lone key defender inside the top bracket of the draft 12 months out, though he plays a more natural role as a rebounder. The SA tall is an excellent kick and sets up play from the last line of defence with instructive ball use. He can intercept with his reading of the play and gets involved in attack up the field.

13. Sam Husband (Tasmania Academy)

Tasmania Devils/Allies

MID, 180cm

The Devils didn't pre-list Husband because they have priority access to Tasmanian in the draft. He's the premier Tassie prospect in their inaugural draft and will be the poster boy of local talent for the 19th team. He's already played two seasons of Talent League football and is at his best using his evasiveness and skills around stoppages.

14. Campbell Creyk

West Perth/Western Australia

MID, 182cm

Creyk surged into the first round mix this year as a contested beast through the midfield. He rips the ball out of stoppages and doesn't often lose one-on-ones, playing with a hard edge that will serve him well at the next level. He will need to round out his game on the outside to continue pushing up draft boards.

15. Taj Garrett

Sturt/South Australia

MID, 183cm

A hard-running midfielder, Garrett's thirst to find the ball and work to contests is an important facet of his game. He outworks opponents and gets forward of the ball to impact. He may play his best football off a wing in the AFL but will get ample exposure on-ball for Sturt next year.

stories.headline: Revisiting sports and pop culture from GTA V's launch
stories.summary: "Grand Theft Auto VI" was released Thursday following a 13-year wait since GTA V.
stories.body:
Peyton Manning was beginning a record-setting season. Joel Embiid had yet to play a college basketball game. And "Breaking Bad" hadn't reached its finale.

That was 4,812 days ago, when "Grand Theft Auto V" arrived on Sept. 17, 2013.

More than 13 years later, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches Thursday, with athletes and teams counting down to its release -- and looking back at how much has changed.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams even quipped during media day that performances could be impacted by the game's release.

"So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet. Just for the month of November, performances are going to go down," Adams said.

Before finding out whether Adams' prediction holds up, here's a look at the sports and pop culture landscape when GTA V arrived -- Sept. 17, 2013.

Seattle and Denver were starting their Super Bowl runs

The NFL had just finished its second week and two squads were in the early stages of dominant campaigns: Seattle and Denver.

The Seahawks' defense proved to be its superpower, earning the "Legion of Boom" nickname. Seattle allowed 273.6 yards and 14.4 points per game, both the fewest in the regular season. The Broncos averaged a league-high 457.3 yards and 37.9 points per game, while Peyton Manning tossed an NFL record 5,477 yards plus 55 touchdowns.

Both teams would finish with 13-3 records, setting up a Super Bowl meeting in February 2014. Seattle would emerge victorious on the biggest stage after stifling Denver's offense in a 43-8 victory -- and the seeds of Super Bowl XLVIII were sprouting as GTA V was released.

Miami Heat looking to three-peat

The LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh Big Three were entering their fourth season as teammates following back-to-back titles.

Miami edged out the San Antonio Spurs in the 2013 NBA Finals, an instant classic. The Heat faced a series clinching defeat in Game 6 before Ray Allen's late 3-pointer sent it into overtime. The extra period ended in a Miami victory to force a Game 7, where it closed out another championship.

The Heat faced the Spurs in a rematch in 2014, and San Antonio got its revenge this time around. But, for two straight summers, Miami reigned supreme.

Five stars preparing to go one-and-done

The 2013 college basketball freshman class had its fair share of heavy hitters.

In March 2013, then-high schoolers Andrew Wiggins and Jabari Parker graced the cover of Slam Magazine with the headline "Young Money: The game's next superstars have arrived." Wiggins and Parker were No. 1 and 2, respectively, in the SC Next rankings, but they were far from the only top prospects.

Joel Embiid, Julius Randle and Aaron Gordon all featured in the top 10 of the rankings as five-star prospects. Each of them, alongside Wiggins and Parker, went one-and-done and were selected in the top 10 of the 2014 NBA draft. Other notable names in the 2013 high school class included twins Aaron and Andrew Harrison, Noah Vonleh and Wayne Selden.

'Breaking Bad' nears its end as 'Roar' rules the charts

One of the greatest TV shows of all time, the final season of "Breaking Bad" aired as GTA V came out.

Two days before its release, the iconic "Ozymandias" episode aired. Series creator Vince Gilligan said that the episode is the "best episode we ever have had or ever will have." It remains one of the highest-rated episodes of the series on IMDB with 9.5 stars.

Pop songs led the way on the Billboard Hot 100 the week GTA V came out. Katy Perry's "Roar" hit No. 1 on Sept. 16, 2013, at the time matching Rihanna for the most No. 1's in the chart's 21-year history at 10. It took six weeks for "Roar" to reach No. 1, then-the fastest No. 1 hit since Perry's "California Gurls" in 2010.

Slotted in at No. 2 was "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell. That track spent 10 weeks on the top before being dethroned. Lorde's "Royals" was at No. 3, while Jay-Z and Justin Timberlake's "Holy Grail" sat at No. 4.

The rest of the songs on the charts' top 10 included: "Wake Me Up!" by Avicii, "Summertime Sadness" by Lana Del Rey vs. Cedric Gervais, "Applause" by Lady Gaga, "Hold On, We're Going Home" by Drake featuring Majid Jordan, "Safe And Sound" by Capital Cities and "Berzerk" by Eminem.

WNBA, MLB teams were building championship legacies

The Minnesota Lynx won their second WNBA championship in 2013, and it would mark the beginning of a dynasty. Minnesota won two more in 2015 and 2017, the latter of which made it four titles in seven seasons as the club also won in 2011. Hall of Famer Maya Moore played a key role in each of the four championships. In 2013, she averaged 20.9 points on 53% shooting in the playoffs.

MLB saw similar dominance in alternating years from the San Francisco Giants. San Francisco missed the postseason in 2013 after World Series titles in 2010 and 2012. Someone privy to a trend could've predicted that the Giants would win it again in 2014 -- which they did. San Francisco hasn't won a World Series since, however.

BCS era coming to a close

College athletics looked entirely different 13 years ago, to say the least.

One of the biggest changes in college football lies in the implementation of the playoff system. Previously, the sport used the BCS rankings for 16 years to determine which two teams would play in the national championship game. That system had its fair share of controversies and came to a close following the 2013 campaign.

Florida State and Auburn made sure the BCS era went out with a bang at the Rose Bowl. Facing a four-point deficit with 1:05 left, Heisman-winning quarterback Jameis Winston led the Seminoles down the field for a game-winning touchdown. Two plays later Florida State closed it out to win 34-31 and clinch its first national championship since 1999 in memorable fashion.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.
